item.title: Silver inflows likely to rebound as import curbs eased for Diwali
item.description: Fresh import permits are set to ease India's silver supply constraints and premiums ahead of Diwali, though demand is expected to trail last year's levels ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: India’s silver imports are set to rebound in time for the busiest jewelry-buying season after the government issued a raft of new permits, easing restrictions that had stifled shipments to one of the world’s biggest markets. Traders and bank dealers this week received quotas covering as much as 6,000 tonnes of silver, said according to four people familiar with the matter. The permits are valid for six months, said the people, who asked not to be named because they’re not allowed to speak publicly. The new licences “should be able to easily cover any demand spike,” said Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Ltd, a precious metals consultancy. “As a result, we no longer see a tight market and premiums are likely to ease substantially in the run-up to Diwali.” India imports almost all of its silver. The government  introduced new licensing requirements in May, one of a number of measures taken to preserve foreign-exchange reserves and defend the rupee.  Would-be silver buyers must now apply for a permit, and every shipment must be accompanied by a certificate proving the country of origin. The government also more than doubled import taxes on gold and silver, adding to the cost of buying. As a result, silver imports initially plunged to a fraction of the country’s demand. In June, monthly shipments hit a three-year low of just 37 tonnes. That rose to 328 tonnes in September, according to an estimate by Metals Focus, as a limited num­ber of permits were granted.  Demand for precious metals typically rises during the festival season that peaks with Diwali. With the latest permits granted, premiums paid to secure silver are likely to ease substantially, Barot said. Indian premiums dropped to around 50 cents an ounce over the global benchmark on Thursday, said Monal Thakkar, managing director of Ashoka Global FZCO, a precious metals trader. That was down from around $2 last week, data from Metals Focus shows. Last year, India imported over 7,000 tonnes of silver, a massive wave of buying that helped to trigger a historic short squeeze in the global market. Prices rose further as speculators piled in — hitting a record high above $121 an ounce in January — before slumping after the West Asia war sent energy prices surging, stoking global inflation fears. Spot silver was trading around $56 an ounce on Thursday. While demand has picked up ahead of the festival season, silver consumption is expected to pale in comparison with last year. Stocking by retailers and wholesalers has been subdued, Barot said, and fewer Indians are gifting silver this year. “We have not seen any meaningful dip-buying despite the price correction, as many investors are sitting on losses from silver bought last year,” he added.  Restrictions lifted Traders, bank dealers have received quotas covering as much as 6,000 tonnes of silverThe Centre introduced licensing requirements in May as a measure to conserve Fx reservesAs a result, silver imports initially plunged to a fraction of the country’s demandDespite demand uptick, silver consumption is expected to pale in comparison with last year

item.title: Sebi warns investors against fraudulent WhatsApp stock tip groups
item.description: The market regulator warned that unregistered entities use invitation-only WhatsApp groups, fabricated profit testimonials and overseas numbers to lure unsuspecting investors ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday cautioned investors against unregistered entities offering stock tips and trading calls through invitation-only WhatsApp groups, warning of misleading profit claims and fraudulent practices. The operators, often using overseas numbers, pose as market experts and encourage members to post fabricated profit testimonials to create an impression of credibility. Sebi said members are frequently invited to new groups through messages from different numbers after the original groups are suspended or banned. The regulator advised investors to avoid acting on such tips, transferring money to suggested platforms or sharing trading account details, and to deal only with Sebi-registered intermediaries.  Mkt regulator allows margin relief against early pay-in of securities The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday said that clearing corporations will not collect margins from trading and clearing members on clients’ subsequent buy or sell positions in the cash segment, up to the value of securities for which early pay-in (EPI) has been successfully accepted. It aims to provide margin relief to clients who have a net sell obligation in a settlement and have completed the EPI process through the clearing corporation.  BSE widens IPO fast-tracking to top 30 firms BSE Index Services will fast-track IPOs ranked among the top 30 companies into its indices, up from the top 10 at present. The change, effective October 23, applies to all broad and market-cap indices except the BSE AllCap Index, the circular said. For the AllCap, Size and Sector indices, IPOs in the top 30 by average daily total market capitalisation will be added with five days’ notice to clients.  Nippon Life India AMC Q2 profit drops 6% Nippon Life India Asset Management on Thursday reported a 6 per cent decline in profit after tax at ₹324.4 crore for September quarter primarily driven by a one-time exceptional item of ₹96.76 crore pertaining to Sebi settlement proceedings. The company earned a profit after tax of ₹344.64 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations surged 21 per cent to ₹796 crore in the quarter.

Jio Platforms IPO: Retail quota full, subscribed 3.47 times on day two The $3.2 billion IPO drew bids for 3.47 times the shares on offer on its second day, led by qualified institutional buyers whose quota was subscribed 9.42 times, exchange data showed

Image: Bloomberg

Reuters Mumbai 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 12:13 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Appetite for the $3.2 billion IPO of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms kept building on Thursday, its second day of public bidding, with orders at 3.47 times the shares up for grabs and the retail portion now fully subscribed, exchange data showed. In what is set to be India's largest IPO and the first by Reliance in 20 years, the listing is a key plank of Ambani's long-term vision to turn Reliance from an oil-and-chemicals giant into an "everything company" spanning consumer, retail and technology. Institutional investors have led demand, with qualified institutional buyers bidding for 9.42 times their quota, exchange data showed. Retail investors, for whom around a third of the issue is reserved, covered their own portion in full by the first two hours of bidding on day two.

item.title: RBI rejects all bids at govt's T-bill auction as short-term yields surge
item.description: The RBI rejected all bids at the Rs 23,000 crore Treasury bill auction as short-term yields climbed, while the benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose to 7.44%.
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday rejected all bids at the government’s treasury-bill (T-bill) auction, signalling discomfort with the sharp rise in short-term borrowing costs, dealers said. The yield on the benchmark 10-year government bond settled at 7.44 per cent, its highest level since November 4, 2022, against the previous close of 7.39 per cent. The central bank last rejected bids in June, when it cancelled auctions of 182-day and 364-day T-bills. At the end of March, it had rejected bids across all three maturities. The government had planned to raise ₹23,000 crore through the sale of 91-day, 182-day and 364-day T-bills. Traders said the yields sought by investors may have been higher than the RBI’s expectations. Government bonds, already under selling pressure due to rising crude oil prices and US treasury yields, were impacted further after the auction result. “The yield (on the benchmark 10-year government bond) will now inch up to 7.50 per cent from here. Crude remains the main overhang, with Brent trading around $112 per barrel, and US yields have also inched up. That is a worry for the market. Sentiment turned negative again after the auction result was announced,” said a dealer at a primary dealership. Cutoff yields on T-bills have risen sharply over the past five weeks. Between September 9 and October 14, yields on 91-day, 182-day and 364-day bills rose by 64 basis points (bps), 83 bps and 69 bps, respectively. At last week’s auction, the government raised funds at yields of 5.73 per cent for 91-day bills, 6.29 per cent for 182-day bills and 6.49 per cent for 364-day bills. The spread between the yield on 364-day T-bills and the RBI’s policy repo rate widened to 99 bps last week, its highest level in four years, reflecting rising short-term borrowing costs.  The central bank has turned decisively hawkish. It raised the repo rate to 5.50 per cent this month and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening, signalling the possibility of further increases. Bets on a 50 bps hike in December are growing, while the benchmark 10-year bond yield has risen around 20 bps since the policy announcement. Liquidity, which had cushioned the market for much of the year, has dried up. The RBI’s latest data showed that net liquidity in the banking system stood at a surplus of around ₹48,303 crore on Tuesday. Consequently, the RBI’s overnight variable rate repo (VRR) auction witnessed strong demand, with bids amounting to ₹93,241 crore against the notified amount of ₹50,000 crore. The weighted average call rate (WACR), the operating target of monetary policy, settled at 5.64 per cent on Wednesday, close to the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate, against 5.66 per cent in the previous session. On Monday, the RBI had conducted a ₹1 trillion VRR auction, the first in three months. “Liquidity has almost dried up, keeping overnight rates elevated. We also have tax outflows coming. The RBI would like to keep overnight rates aligned with the repo rate. That is why it is conducting these temporary liquidity infusions,” said a dealer at a state-owned bank. The turnaround in liquidity has been sharp. The RBI had been in absorption mode since August 6, following its last VRR auction on July 29, as liquidity had swelled due to Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank, or FCNR(B), deposit swaps with the central bank. Since then, the daily cash reserve requirement has been tightened from October 16. Average daily net absorption under the liquidity adjustment facility rose from ₹1.2 trillion in July to ₹5.8 trillion in August. As recently as October 12, the RBI absorbed a net ₹3.36 trillion, while the call rate stood at 5.41 per cent. The central bank plans to conduct another overnight VRR auction worth ₹50,000 crore on Thursday.
